title: Dancehall
tagline: A sharper, more rhythmic strain of Jamaican music with a direct club focus.
summary: Dancehall pushes reggae toward faster tempos, louder drums and a more immediate, vocal-forward presentation. It often feels social and kinetic, built for movement and for direct interaction between performer and crowd. The style grew quickly in Jamaica and then spread into a wider global club circuit.

pillars.name: Shabba Ranks
pillars.why: Shabba Ranks helped define dancehall’s vocal power and its ability to turn rhythm into a direct social force.

pillars.name: Super Cat
pillars.why: Super Cat brought a sharp lyrical precision and a strong sense of vocal style to the form.

pillars.name: Beenie Man
pillars.why: Beenie Man made dancehall feel globally legible while keeping the music rooted in its local energy.
